A1.justification: Both PDFs describe GS-ID, with substantial shared content despite retitling and methodological revision. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and support comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original GS-ID results on TensoIR Synthetic and Mip-NeRF 360, ablations, and appendix evaluations on DeepBlending and Tanks & Temples.

after.justification: V2 reports original revised GS-ID results, including ADT evaluation, shadow and prior ablations, and measurements of training time and GPU memory.

M1.justification: V1's 2DGS pipeline with Omnidata, Intrinsic Image Diffusion, and baked ambient occlusion becomes a 3DGS pipeline using RGB↔X priors, learned per-splat shadow visibility, and inference-time shadow mapping. V2 also introduces depth-masked normal supervision and revises lighting/material objectives. SG mixtures, grid initialization, light-position optimization, pruning, and deferred shading already existed in v1.

E1.justification: V2 adds controlled material and illumination evaluation on four ADT-derived scanned objects: Donut, Figurine, Birdhouse, and Table. This substantially extends reference-based intrinsic evaluation beyond the retained TensoIR synthetic objects. Mip-NeRF 360, DeepBlending, and Tanks & Temples remain represented, including in the appendices.

E2.justification: The TensoIR comparison adds GaussianShader and Relightable 3D Gaussian, labeled RelightGS/R3DG, and removes NeRFactor; the appendix's per-scene comparison also drops NeRFactor. GaussianShader's earlier participation on Mip-NeRF 360 does not negate its addition here. V1's aggregate Mip-NeRF comparison containing NeRF and Deep Blending also disappears, although overlapping per-scene comparisons remain.

E3.justification: The reported training budget changes from 30k reconstruction iterations plus baking and 30k illumination iterations to a principally described 20k-plus-10k schedule. V2 adds roughness MSE, rendered roughness ground truth, and an evaluation-specific radiance formula dividing environmental output by albedo (Eq. 12). These substantially revise evaluation settings, although conflicting appendix statements leave the exact executed schedule uncertain.

E4.justification: V2 Table 3 adds controls removing all priors, removing the shadow field, and using a single SGM. Its quantitative NVS ablations concern TensoIR rather than v1's Mip-NeRF 360 results. Table 4 adds training-time scaling and CUDA-memory comparisons. These extend the retained individual-prior, lighting-component, and forward-versus-deferred shading analyses.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental run or seed counts, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. V2's expanded tables continue reporting point estimates; its references to different initializations do not establish a statistical evaluation procedure.

E6.justification: TensoIR Table 1 changes GS-ID's NVS PSNR from 36.72 to 39.13 and normal MAE from 4.120 to 4.602. These are results for revised methods/settings, not controlled same-setting gains. ADT, roughness, quantitative relighting, efficiency, and additional ablation entries are added. Stage-1 result rows disappear, while the appendix's final-stage DeepBlending and Tanks & Temples values are retained.

T1.justification: V2 removes the SH-based occlusion reconstruction and introduces a formal sigmoid visibility model, depth-masked normal objective, and revised rendering/evaluation equations. The positional regularizer changes substantively from a sum of reciprocal distances in v1 Eq. 10 to a sum of max(d_min-d_max, 0) terms in v2 Eq. 4. These change the mathematical formulation rather than merely its notation.

C1.justification: V2 presents an end-to-end 3DGS framework and makes visibility-aware deshadowing a central contribution; direct-light shadow handling was future work in v1's conclusion. It removes v1's explicit claim of being first to introduce diffusion priors for geometry/material estimation. The broader claims of illumination decomposition and editable lighting remain.

C2.justification: V2 qualifies normal-prior reliability in distant regions, explains TensoIR's lower normal error through its continuous MLP representation, and introduces an anisotropy/storage limitation. It drops v1's out-of-distribution-prior caveat and area-light future-work discussion. These revise specific interpretations and limitations while retaining the central rationale for priors and separated lighting.

D1.justification: V2 newly specifies RTX 4090 hardware, a 3×3×3 light grid, 16 SGs per mixture, initialization bounds, shadow/pruning constants, and CUDA chunking. V1's explicit source-code link is removed. Reproducibility is complicated by new contradictions: main-text Eq. 8 uses L2 without metallic supervision, appendix Eq. 15 uses L1 including metallic, and post-reconstruction training is variously stated as 10k or 15k iterations.

R1.justification: V2 adds a substantive Lighting Models discussion contrasting unknown illumination with calibrated near/far-field capture and editable explicit lighting with implicit light fields. Newly cited and discussed work includes VMINer, GS3, DN-Splatter, and NeILF/NeILF++. This substantially expands positioning beyond v1's geometry-reconstruction and intrinsic-decomposition discussion.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, contribution list, methodology, and conclusion are extensively rewritten. The narrative changes from three chronological stages to numbered sections organized around lighting, deshadowing, and diffusion priors. The standalone preliminaries disappear, and implementation and experimental discussions are reorganized across the main text and supplement.

P2.justification: V2 redesigns the opening illustration and pipeline, adds SGM and shadow schematics, expands Table 1 with roughness, relighting, and timing columns, and adds ADT and efficiency displays. The ambient-occlusion baking diagram is removed. Several appendix displays are retained or revised rather than newly introduced; the final light-editing and composition images are retained with renumbering.

improvement.justification: V2 addresses v1's explicit shadow-handling limitation and adds useful evidence: Table 3 reports albedo PSNR of 33.493 with the shadow field versus 30.280 without it, alongside new ADT, roughness, relighting, and efficiency evaluations. However, newly conflicting loss definitions and training durations make the evaluated procedure difficult to reproduce. ADT summary albedo scores also have unexplained differences from the per-scene arithmetic means in Table 12. These problems affect interpretation of the expanded evidence, so the substantial benefits do not establish a reliable net quality direction.
